nodes.label: The particle-to-grid handoff is exact and volume-correct: the histogram total...
nodes.statement: The particle-to-grid handoff is exact and volume-correct: the histogram total never differs from the molecule count (mismatch = 0 molecules at every record), and uniformly distributed particles bin to a uniform concentration across node classes (max |z| = 0.48; corner and edge concentrations 1.0034× and 1.0019× interior, both within 0.4%), confirming the 1/4-corner and 1/2-edge element-volume convention.

nodes.label: decision/derived-two-way-exchange-fl1
The native VCell embedded solver diverges strongly and the divergence is full...
nodes.statement: The native VCell embedded solver diverges strongly and the divergence is fully explained by a known defect: native creation is 1.813× the expectation, matching the predicted full-volume boundary overproduction Σ(full)/Σ(actual)=1.815× to 0.1% (ratio 0.999). As a consequence native (A+B) grows 177% in 5 s and its steady-state ratio is 51% off, so the two solvers disagree at |z| ≈ 219 (totals) / 153 (profile). This is vcell-fvsolver's bug (virtualcell/vcell-fvsolver#24), not the coupling method.

nodes.label: Plain process-bigraph "start-of-interval" scheduling roughly halves the coupl...
nodes.statement: Plain process-bigraph "start-of-interval" scheduling roughly halves the coupling error at large k (0.0049 at k=16, 0.0110 at k=32 vs 0.0110 and 0.0218 for fvsolver mode; fitted order 0.80), because reading the field at the start of the particle step partly cancels the PDE side's lag. vcell-fvsolver's fixed ordering cannot use this without changing the solver.

nodes.label: The process-bigraph framework overhead is bounded and small: at most 2.97 mil...
nodes.statement: The process-bigraph framework overhead is bounded and small: at most 2.97 milliseconds per step across all configurations (the bound is 10 milliseconds), ranging from 3.5% of co-sim time on the heaviest problem (200k particles) up to 41.7% on the smallest (2k particles on 21×21×3), where there is little real work to amortize it against.

nodes.label: The modular co-simulation is faster than the native embedded solve in every c...
nodes.statement: The modular co-simulation is faster than the native embedded solve in every configuration: co-sim/native-solve ranges from 0.25× (2k particles) to 0.93× on the largest grid (81×81×3), and 0.69× at 200k particles (co-sim 2.64 s vs native solve 3.82 s). The decomposition costs nothing at scale — well under the 2× bound.

nodes.label: Co-sim time shifts cleanly with the workload: particles dominate at high part...
nodes.statement: Co-sim time shifts cleanly with the workload: particles dominate at high particle counts (95.9% of co-sim time at 200k particles, PDE only 0.8%), while the PDE dominates on the largest grid (49.7% at 81×81×3). Framework overhead is largest precisely where total work is smallest (41.7% at 2k particles), as expected for a fixed per-step scheduling cost.
